headline: Chai Discovery, a start-up that uses AI to design drug molecules, has signed a collaboration with drugmaker GSK after GSK tested its designs in the laboratory.
score_reason: A new deal with a major drugmaker backed by a lab test, but the results are the companies' own statements and no drug has resulted yet.
importance_line: Drug developers and, in the long run, patients may gain faster ways to find new medicines, but the lab results come from the companies themselves and no treatment has been shown.
summary: Contract Pharma reports that Chai Discovery announced a collaboration with GSK after GSK tested Chai's AI-made molecule designs in its own laboratories and, Chai says, found binders to all the targets tested. Endpoints News counts it as Chai's sixth deal with a drug company in nine months; the results are the two companies' own statements and no independent review is reported.
notes: A binder is a molecule that attaches to a chosen target in the body; the AI designs these. The Endpoints News exclusive (pool link) is paywalled, so the text was read at Contract Pharma, which carries Chai's announcement; the sixth-partner count comes from the Endpoints headline only. 'Not independently reviewed' reflects that no outside review is reported.
